decision: One distinct incoming-unwanted-events repair guide is justified; do not append an unrelated micro-FAQ to outgoing sharing or make separate synonym pages.
userTask: Identify an unwanted incoming invitation versus an unwanted subscribed calendar, use the owning provider’s appropriate report/unsubscribe route, and separately review future invitation settings without deleting the wrong calendar.

observedVsInferred.observed: Current Apple and Google provider pages explicitly document different reporting, subscription removal and invitation filtering workflows. Five relevant complete current English guides do not teach this incoming repair decision.
observedVsInferred.inferred: A coherent reader need suitable for one guide; demand size and commercial priority are not measured.

facts: Google reporting requires a Google Calendar-sent event; other-provider events are outside this reporting feature.
Reporting a recurring event removes the series from the reporting calendar.
Google iPhone app provides a known-sender invitation setting. Known includes contacts, organization and prior interaction; it may reveal sender is not a contact.
primaryReads.boundary: Google app controls, not Cloud controls.

primaryReads.discovery: Followed link7 from the Google iOS report guide.
facts: Changes apply only to new invitations; work/school administrators may restrict available settings.
Known-sender or email-response modes control automatic calendar addition; email may still arrive.
Pending invitation visibility for existing authorized viewers is a separate option.
primaryReads.boundary: Computer instructions; do not label all menus iPhone menus or promise spam elimination.

facts: This current version explicitly scopes instructions to iOS26 or later.
Apple Calendar distinguishes deleting an event/reporting unknown-contact junk, calendar deletion/unsubscribe, and merely hiding a calendar.
primaryReads.boundary: Do not recommend Delete Calendar as interchangeable with unsubscribing. Identify actual source first; not Cloud menu instructions.

recommendedNextAction.type: Prepare one substantive provider-led draft for independent review before integration
outline: Identify original calendar/account and whether this is an invitation, subscribed feed or owned/imported event. Do not follow suspicious event links.
Apple Calendar iOS26+ report versus unsubscribe versus hide, with source identification before removal.
Google reporting eligibility and recurring-series consequence.
Future Google invitations: new-only change, administrator limits, known-sender/email-response distinction.
iCloud web reporting on tablet/computer and correct Apple Account.
Recheck original provider and selected calendar; hiding is not removal. Route account disconnect and secret-feed exposure to existing guides.
recommendedNextAction.productBoundary: No Cloud Report Junk, blocking, anti-spam, subscription-removal or identical-settings capability is established by this research. Keep provider operations explicitly attributed. No native audit or customer operations performed.
recommendedNextAction.scenario: Unfamiliar appointments began after opening a calendar link. First determine whether they belong to a subscribed calendar; repeatedly deleting visible appointments or disconnecting the entire Google account is not the diagnosis.
